acceptanceCovered: A project-local skill defines the standard and is tracked by git (not swallowed by the .gitignore skill opt-in list) -- proven: `.claude/skills/write-unit-tests-and-storybook-stories/SKILL.md` is in `git ls-files` output and `git check-ignore` exits 1 (not ignored); `.gitignore` gained the explicit `!.claude/skills/write-unit-tests-and-storybook-stories/` un-ignore line.

Every hook, util, helper, Server Action and designated Route Handler in the coverage allowlist has a co-located unit test file -- proven: read every allowlisted source and its sibling test (lib/supabase/client.ts+.test.ts, server.ts+.test.ts, proxy-client.ts+.test.ts, next-path.ts+.test.ts, hooks/use-login-actions.ts+.test.ts, hooks/use-menu-keyboard-nav.ts+.test.ts, app/actions/locale.ts+.test.ts, app/todo/actions.ts+.test.ts, app/auth/callback/route.ts+.test.ts) -- all present and co-located, none placed under a __tests__/ folder.

Unit-test coverage reaches 100% for statements, branches, functions and lines across the allowlist, and the threshold genuinely fails the process below that rather than only printing a number -- proven by orchestrator's temper-results.json: 100/100/100/100 measured, and deleting one describe block reproduced a real non-zero exit (98.26% branches < 100% threshold). `vitest.config.ts:100` has `thresholds: { 100: true }`.

UI components are exempt from unit tests, and that exemption is achieved structurally by the allowlist carrying no .tsx glob rather than by a maintained exclude list -- proven: `vitest.config.ts` coverage.include (lines 82-88) lists only `lib/**/*.ts`, `hooks/**/*.ts`, `app/actions/**/*.ts`, `app/todo/actions.ts`, `app/auth/callback/route.ts` -- grepped the whole file, zero `.tsx` glob anywhere in `include`.

Every common component, judged by a mechanically checkable content test, has a co-located Storybook story documenting its main variants -- proven: applied the skill's 3-question test to every .tsx in components/ (find components -type f -name '*.tsx'); the 7 components that pass (GoogleLoginButton, LanguageSelector, LoginErrorAlert, LoginFooter, IconDown, IconGoogle, IconVnFlag) each have a .stories.tsx with multiple variant exports (e.g. GoogleLoginButton: Default+Pending; LanguageSelector: Vietnamese+English+Open with a real click-driven `play` function); the 3 that fail the test (LoginHeader, LoginHero -- both assemble >=2 named components; LoginBackground -- hardcodes its own image, no props) correctly have none.

Each main route that renders presentational UI has one viewable Storybook story that needs no login, no dev server and no live Supabase instance -- proven: login-screen.stories.tsx and todo-screen.stories.tsx both mock their callbacks as no-ops and pass static copy, no network/auth dependency; `/` is exempt (redirect-only, no JSX, confirmed against the skill table).

One shared MSW handler module serves both the vitest Node runtime and the Storybook browser runtime, with no duplicate handler for the same endpoint -- proven: grepped every .ts/.tsx for `http.get(`/`http.post(` outside test files -- only `mocks/handlers.ts` defines handlers (3: /auth/v1/token, /auth/v1/user, /auth/v1/logout); `mocks/node.ts` and `.storybook/preview.tsx` both import from that one module; the only `server.use(...)` override is a single per-test scoped 400-response variant in route.test.ts, cleaned up by the shared `afterEach(() => server.resetHandlers())` in tests/setup/msw-node.ts.

The existing e2e suite still passes, and the extraction of TodoScreen from app/todo/page.tsx changes no markup, no className and does not weaken the authoritative auth guard -- proven: diffed page.tsx against b7254e5 -- the createClient()->getUser()->if(!user) redirect('/login') sequence is byte-identical and unconditional, executed before getTranslations/render exactly as before; diffed the extracted JSX against the pre-extraction JSX in the old page.tsx -- the <main>/<h1>/<form>/<button> tree, every className, and every attribute are verbatim, only greeting/logout copy swapped for greeting/logoutLabel props; TodoScreen carries no 'use client' directive and is not async. 27/27 CI-safe e2e recorded passing in temper-results.json.

lint, format check, unit tests with coverage, build, typecheck and the Storybook build all exit 0 -- accepted per orchestrator's temper-results.json (all six commands exit 0); re-verified the CI workflow wiring matches (ci.yml now runs `pnpm test:unit:coverage` and a `Build Storybook` step in the quality job).
regressionChecked: app/todo/page.tsx is the only production runtime file modified -- walked it line by line against b7254e5's version: guard order/logic unchanged, only the render body now delegates to <TodoScreen>. No access-control or markup regression found.

vitest.config.ts changes what the coverage number measures -- confirmed include list has no .tsx glob (see acceptance criterion 4 above); the allowlist is exactly the 5 entries the plan specifies, nothing wider.

The CI quality job swapped pnpm test:unit for pnpm test:unit:coverage and gained a Build Storybook step -- confirmed via `git diff` on .github/workflows/ci.yml: both changes present, Storybook step placed after typecheck per the file's own ordering comment.

public/mockServiceWorker.js is generated and served from public/, and is excluded from eslint -- confirmed the file is msw's standard `/* Please do NOT modify this file. */` boilerplate (PACKAGE_VERSION 2.15.0 matching package.json's pinned msw version) and eslint.config.mjs's ignore list gained the exact `public/mockServiceWorker.js` line.
tsconfig.json gained .storybook globs -- confirmed `.storybook/**/*.ts` and `.storybook/**/*.tsx` were added to tsconfig's include array.

No database, migration, API contract or user-facing product behavior changed -- confirmed: the only behavioral file (page.tsx) preserves guard order and JSX verbatim; no migration files, no exported API route signature changed; the /auth/callback route.ts source itself is untouched, only tested.

findings.summary: This branch's history also carries an unrelated CLAUDE.md rewrite (--flow flag, gh --repo pinning, decisions/action-items protocol) with no connection to the testing/Storybook standard the plan describes. Harmless (project meta config, not shipped code) but it is scope creep on this diff and slightly muddies a review focused on the testing standard.
